newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ regulator warns power firms over contract terms.
newsitem.headline: NZ regulator warns power firms over contract terms.

text.p: New Zealand's Commerce Commission said on Friday it was giving a preliminary warning to 29 power companies that their contracts for supplying electricity to domestic customers did not comply with rules on providing guarantees and remedies.

Companies have been reminded of the content of the Consumer Guarantees Act, under which suppliers have an obligation to use reasonable care and skill to supply goods and services and may not limit their liabilities to particular amounts.
Commission chairman Alan Bollard noted that at this stage the panel intended to give the companies time to amend their contracts and withdraw offending clauses.
"It will then follow-up its warnings," he added.
The power companies involved represent the bulk of the minor regional players in the fragmented New Zealand market and some of the larger firms, including Bay of Plenty Electricity.
